checks.after: He had a dragon countenance and plaque-like teeth, and stood seven chi eight cun tall.
checks.reason: 龍顏版齒 and 七尺八寸 are definite wording issues in the EN field: imperial/feet-inches readings understate the physiognomy terms and convert the chi-cun measures.

checks.after: Huang killed Zhao and sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation; they met Ren at Xiandu.
checks.reason: 遇仁於險瀆 follows 遣使按檢, so the literal’s bare ‘met Ren’ wrongly allows Huang as subject; the envoys are the ones who met Ren.

checks.after: Ren knew the affair had come out; he killed Huang’s envoy and returned east to Pingguo.
checks.reason: 知事發, 殺皝使, and 東歸平郭 are under-rendered as plot-exposed/messenger/fled; return-east and Huang’s envoy are required.

checks.after: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and the various Xianbei divisions all backed him.
checks.reason: 鮮卑諸部 means various Xianbei divisions or tribes, not ‘other Xianbei chiefs,’ which invents a chief-class reading.

checks.after: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent his marshal Feng Yi to attack the Xianbei Muti at Bailang, and the Yangwei general Shuyu to attack the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both were beheaded.
checks.reason: 揚威 before 淑虞 is omitted in EN, and 皆斬之 is the paired beheading rather than a vague taking of heads.

checks.after: Liao’s younger brother Lan together with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.
checks.reason: 遼弟蘭 marks Lan as Liao’s younger brother, and 寇/擊敗 are raid and defeat, not an open-ended ‘until driven off.’

checks.after: Huang warned Han, saying: “The bandits’ host is numerous and their spirit keen; it is hard to contend at the spear-tip. You ought to look to complete safety, and carefully do not advance lightly; you must wait until the troops are gathered and the lines set, then strike them.”
checks.reason: The EN quote drops 難與爭鋒, 宜顧萬全, and 慎勿輕進 as distinct admonitions inside Huang’s warning.

checks.after: Han’s nature was fierce and keen; he dispatched over a thousand cavalry as a vanguard to advance; Feng Yi stopped him, but Han did not follow, was defeated by Lan, and the dead were more than half.
checks.reason: 千餘騎 is over a thousand cavalry, 封弈止之 is a stop not a mere warning, and 死者大半 is more than half dead.

checks.after: Sheyiyu led cavalry to pursue battle at the Hun River and was again defeated.
checks.reason: After Feng Yi’s prior victory, 又敗之 records Sheyiyu’s further defeat, not Sheyiyu defeating ‘them.’

checks.after: Huang said, “Formerly the sea water had no ice; since Ren’s rebellion, the freeze has joined three times.
checks.reason: 舊海水無淩 is no ice formerly, not ‘seldom froze,’ and 凍合者三矣 is three joinings of the freeze.

checks.after: Ren did not expect Huang’s arrival; the army was seven li from Pingguo when scout riders reported it; Ren came out to fight in confusion, was captured by Huang, who killed Ren and returned.
checks.reason: 軍去平郭七里 is the army, 候騎乃告 is omitted, and 殺仁而還 must keep the killing-and-return close.

checks.after: Duan Liao sent general Li Yong to night-raid Wuxing; meeting rain, he withdrew; commandant Zhang Meng pursued and captured Yong.
checks.reason: 遣將李詠 names the sent general, 引還 is withdraw, and 都尉張萌 is omitted in the EN compression.

checks.after: He sent Feng Yi leading light cavalry in pursuit; Feng defeated them, gathered their military stores, lodged on their grain for twenty days, and returned.
checks.reason: EN omits 遣, the defeat 敗之, and 而還 after the twenty-day 館穀 lodging on enemy grain.

checks.after: He sent concurrent chief clerk Liu Bin and palace director Yang Jing to escort Xu Meng and others back to the capital.
checks.reason: 兼長史 and 郎中令 are explicit offices for Liu Bin and Yang Jing that the EN field drops.

checks.after: He had his heir apparent Jun campaign against Duan Liao’s cities, and Feng Yi attack a separate Yuwen division; both returned in great victory.
checks.reason: 攻宇文別部 is a separate Yuwen division, not undifferentiated ‘the Yuwen,’ and 使其/伐 structure is flattened.

checks.after: He later relocated Changli commandery, built Haocheng east of Yilian, and had general Lan Bo garrison it to press Yilian.
checks.reason: 徙昌黎郡 relocates Changli commandery rather than Huang’s own seat, and 將軍/以逼乙連 are omitted.

checks.after: Liao sent general Qu Yun to attack Xingguo; Yun fought a great battle with Huang’s general Murong Zun at Wuguan River, was defeated and beheaded, and his entire force was captured.
checks.reason: 遼遣將 and 皝將 are omitted, and 雲敗，斬之 is defeat then beheading rather than a vague ‘destroyed.’

checks.after: He made his wife Lady Duan queen and the heir apparent Jun crown prince, all following the Wei Wu and Jin Wen precedents of assisting in government.
checks.reason: 其妻 and 世子 are explicit, and 輔政故事 is the assisting-government precedent, not a bare Cao Cao/Sima Zhao name citation.

checks.after: Shi Hu entered Lingzhi, furious that Huang had not joined forces, advanced to strike him as far as Jicheng; several hundred thousand troops attacked from all four sides, and thirty-six cities among the prefectures, counties, and various divisions rebelled in response to Shi Hu.
checks.reason: 四面進攻 and 郡縣諸部叛應…三十六城 are definite omissions beyond coordinated advance and bare ‘towns.’

checks.after: Sent his son Ke and others leading two thousand cavalry; at dawn they sortied and struck them.
checks.reason: 子恪等 is his son Ke and others, not plural ‘sons Ke’; the dawn sortie striking them is required.

checks.after: esteemed
checks.reason: 尚經學 means he esteemed classical learning; relation ‘studied’ understates 尚 as mere study rather than valuing.
